newsitem.title: UK: HSBC's Bootle becomes UK "wise man".
newsitem.headline: HSBC's Bootle becomes UK "wise man".

text.p: Roger Bootle, chief economist at the HSBC Group, will become a member of the UK Treasury's six-member panel of independent economic advisers, the Treasury said.
He will replace Patrick Minford, whose term expires at the end of the year.
Minford has frequently been at odds with other members of the panel, especially with his recent calls for sharp cuts in interest rates and taxes.

Bootle's latest book, "The Death of Inflation," published last April, argued that inflation was virtually dead in major western countries and that this would have a significant impact on government policies and on personal finances.
"We are witnessing the death of perpetual inflation and the beginning of the zero era," he wrote.
The panel produces twice-yearly reports to the Chancellor of the Exchequer on the state of the economy.
The other members of the panel are:

Kate Barker (Confederation of British Industry), Tim Congdon (Lombard Street Research), Gavyn Davies (Goldman Sachs), Bridget Rosewell (Business Strategies) and Martin Weale (National Institute of Economic and Social Research). -- Richard Murphy, London Newsroom 44 171 542 2774
